project: POP PUNK GUITAR LIBRARY MANAGER ULTIMATE

profiles.source_location_note: Resolve the actual folder or archive on the user's PC at first local scan. Do not assume a path or that source audio is present in this repository.

plugin_mapping.purpose: Build source material candidates for POP PUNK GUITAR ULTIMATE factory presets and sub-presets.

output_policy.sample_rate_policy: Preserve source rate unless an explicitly approved conversion is required.

multi_resolution_extraction.strategy: Create linked candidate levels from each source; do not choose only one segmentation size.

levels.purpose: Extract coherent riffs, loops, progressions and multi-bar phrases.
Extract useful rhythmic passages, palm-mute patterns, strumming and chord-hit sequences.
Extract individual notes, chord hits, slides and harmonics when boundaries are reliable.
Detect attacks for analysis; do not publish automatically without review.

boundary_rules: Use onset detection as evidence, not as the sole segmentation rule.
Prefer musical boundaries, beat/bar alignment and phrase coherence when confidence supports them.
Preserve natural attack and decay; handle boundaries to avoid clicks.
Do not split a chord or sustained note in the middle merely because its waveform changes.
Do not split a coherent riff into isolated notes by default; retain both phrase and optional child events.
Keep uncertain boundaries as review candidates with confidence and editable start/end markers.
Detect repetitions and suggest representative takes while retaining meaningful performance variations.

output_policy.plugin_asset_rule: Each approved preset assignment points to a specific derived WAV clip or deliberately selected phrase/loop. The plugin must not play the full source recording unless explicitly selected as the asset.

required_content_families.label: One-shots
required_content_families.inspect: Detect and catalogue every useful isolated hit or short playable sound; preserve attack, body and natural decay.

required_content_families.label: Loops
required_content_families.inspect: Identify complete musical loops and retain each parent loop while creating linked phrase and event candidates.

required_content_families.label: Lead Guitar
required_content_families.inspect: Identify lead lines, melodic phrases, single-note runs, hooks, fills, bends, slides, vibrato, harmonics and sustained lead notes.

required_content_families.label: Palm-muted guitar
required_content_families.inspect: Distinguish palm-muted single notes, chord hits, repeated-note patterns, tight rhythmic parts and mixed muted/open passages.

required_content_families.label: Rhythm Guitar
required_content_families.inspect: Identify downstrokes, upstrokes, alternate strumming, chugging, open chords, power chords, syncopation and full rhythm passages.

required_content_families.label: Chords and progressions
required_content_families.inspect: Identify individual chord hits, chord changes, progressions and coherent multi-bar chord parts without destroying their musical context.

required_content_families.label: Transitions and guitar FX
required_content_families.inspect: Identify slides, swells, pick scrapes, feedback, harmonics, noise effects, transitions, endings and fills.

content_relationship_rules: Classify each useful item by both content family and musical role; a single asset may carry multiple verified tags.
Keep one-shot, loop, lead-guitar and palm-muted material as distinct searchable classifications; do not merge them into a generic guitar category.
For every detected loop, retain the full parent loop and create linked phrase, rhythm-pattern, chord-event and note-event candidates only where boundaries are reliable.
For lead-guitar recordings, preserve complete melodic lines and coherent phrases as well as optional individual note candidates.
For palm-muted material, distinguish muted notes/chords from open or mixed articulation passages.
Record classification confidence and require listening review when the class or articulation is uncertain.
Do not infer musical key, tempo, chord identity or articulation solely from a filename; analyse audio and retain confidence/unknown when uncertain.

style_taxonomy.rule: Treat genre and subgenre as searchable style tags with confidence, not as claims of artist/song identity. One asset may have multiple verified style tags.

chord_analysis.rule: Never force a chord label when the audio is ambiguous, distorted, layered or incomplete; retain unknown/ambiguous and offer listening review.

performance_techniques.rule: Technique labels require audio evidence or explicit trustworthy source metadata; store confidence and review status. Do not infer technique solely from filenames.

effects_and_tone_tags.rule: Separate recorded source tone/effects from plugin processing suggestions. A detected or tagged effect is not automatically proof of the exact hardware or plugin used.
